statement: Fix the prepared parent and a feasible center at a layer j ≤ s. Assume the modified sampler, scalar comparison, and major-decomposition contracts established above. Let G0 be a controlled filtered group of degree r, with a strong rational projection π0 : G0 → Y . Suppose a pre-inverse fraction of the available paths are modular-good in the sense of Equation (6.3), and each such path has a polynomial gψ(v, z) whose logarithmic coordinates have bounded total degree, adapted in v at each fixed z, and satisfy the formal identity π0 gψ(v, z) = PY (Xψ(v, z); z), Xψ = (ψ, β ◦ ψ). (8.1) Here PY (X; z) is fixed on those paths, weighted filtered in X, and polynomial in z, with bounded total degree. There is no bound on the coefficients of either polynomial. Let the two external fields satisfy Definition 8.1. Suppose their signed score, with the original slice mask 1S and full parameter mass, is at least δ > 0: Et1S(t) h 1no bad(t)F− ψ,ψ(t)(θ, e t)(gψ(t)Γ0 ) − λF+ ψ,ψ(t)(θ, e t)(gψ(t)Γ0 ) i ≥ δ, (8.2) 61 where 0 < λ ≤ 1. Include the original slice cost, the short-label range bounds, and log(1/δ) in the prescribed preliminary data. All path probabilities refer to the original ensemble, with discarded paths retained as zero mass; subsequent selections are subsets of the modular-good productive paths just specified. For any prescribed 0 < η < δ/2, include log(1/η) in that request. Then one retained modular-good path admits a stochastic polynomial g♯ (X, θ, e t) ∈ G0 , π0 g♯ (X, θ, e t) = PY (X; z) (8.3) whose K-score, with the same slice and flag masks and the expectation of the two payoffs, is at least δ − η. A stochastic polynomial means a polynomial formula with random constant parameters, sampled independently of its arguments. Its total logarithmic-coordinate degree is bounded in terms of the input degree bounds only; its coefficients need not be bounded. A filtered-degree bound in the original parameters is not asserted. On the joint chart and exact-inactive locus zI(X) = zI(tI), (8.4) each expected payoff separately is independent of the representatives chosen for the parallel residue labels, with all other data fixed. This is a pointwise statement for every admissible label choice. The retained path fraction and all auxiliary logarithmic costs may have cold pre-cost. The number of successive polynomial budget increases and all degree increases depend only on the fixed input degrees. Thus, when δ, the original slice, and η have warm bounds, the resulting score and slice still have those bounds.
